I train, quantize and deploy neural networks that run in real time on a microcontroller, and I handle the whole chain around them, from the board schematic to the firmware. Today at Ocean Data System, I develop the onboard electronics and safety systems used in offshore racing.

missions.title: Embedded firmware
missions.text: Development and maintenance of the onboard systems firmware, in C# on .NET Micro Framework and TinyCLR (400 MHz ARM9 target). A tightly constrained managed runtime: concurrency through threads, timers and locks, non-deterministic garbage collection. Hence producer/consumer ring buffers and allocations kept to a minimum in acquisition loops.

missions.title: Safety systems
missions.text: Heel monitoring and anti-capsize detection, alarms, man overboard, watchdog. Every change is assessed from the degraded-mode angle: an optimisation that weakens an alarm or a fault detection is a defect.

missions.title: Multi-sensor acquisition
missions.text: Inertial attitude unit (AHRS), wireless sensors, CAN keypads: integration on CAN/J1939, NMEA 0183 and NMEA 2000 buses, RS-232/422/485 serial links, Modbus and BLE. Drivers, timestamping, logging and monitoring.

missions.title: Electronics design
missions.text: Schematic and layout in KiCad and Eagle: revisions of production boards and a full redesign of a control board (12/24/48 V supply, second independent CAN port). One product owned from board to firmware: embedded HTTP and FTP servers, Wi-Fi access point, configuration dashboard.

missions.title: Hardware and software debugging
missions.text: The most expensive defects hide at the boundary between the two. Oscilloscope and logic analyser, bus integrity, noisy supply, datasheets checked against real conditions (switching time versus bit time) — then the fix, in the firmware or on the board.

missions.title: Production, commissioning, support
missions.text: Assembly, soldering and testing before shipping; onboard integration and validation; remote diagnosis with crews, skippers and shipyards. The same rigour on the phone as in the lab.

current.side: On the side: internal local-AI tooling — a document indexing and search agent built on a local LLM (Ollama), and a feasibility study for on-premise generative AI.

points: Designed a complete embedded UWB radar chain, from raw signal acquisition to decision: preprocessing, FFT, feature extraction and real-time CNN classification on an ARM Cortex-M33.
Reimplemented in C the processing chain first prototyped in Python, to fit the real-time and memory constraints of the target and remove the dependency on a host PC.
Training, INT8 quantization and on-target deployment of the models, trading off inference latency, memory footprint and detection quality.
Field measurement campaigns, analysis of the gap between laboratory and real conditions, technical documentation in English with international teams.
End-to-end Edge AI workflow: sensor acquisition, model training, quantization and deployment on the eIQ Neutron NPU.
Inference optimisation on constrained targets, comparison of NPU against CPU execution, and writing of the deployment guide used internally.
Distributed embedded architecture (Arduino Mega and Raspberry Pi 4) for a tracked mobile robot with a 6-axis arm, YOLOv5 computer vision for object detection and MQTT-monitored autonomous charging.

about.label: About
about.title: From signal to decision, from schematic to the field
about.photo_alt: Portrait of Ali Azami holding an ENSEEIHT envelope
bio: An engineer with two degrees — ENSEEIHT in Toulouse (electronics and AI for embedded systems) and EHTP in Casablanca (electrical engineering) — I work where software meets physics: a signal to acquire, memory counted in kilobytes, a real-time deadline to meet.

At Schaeffler and NXP, I carried complete embedded AI chains, from radar acquisition to inference on a microcontroller. At Ocean Data System, the scope widened to the whole product: the board, the firmware, commissioning and support, for equipment that has to hold at sea with no possible intervention.

What drives me: taking a hard problem, understanding what the measurement really says, and building the whole chain until it works in the field. Where I am heading: embedded AI, specifically — designing, optimising and deploying models on constrained targets.

method.title: Facts before interpretation
method.text: I restate the symptom before looking for a solution, and I only conclude on a demonstrated cause.

method.title: Measure rather than estimate
method.text: Latency, memory, detection rate: every result is measured on the target, not assumed.

method.title: Think degraded mode
method.text: What goes to sea cannot be patched remotely. Every change comes with the list of what must be retested.

method.title: From the lab to the field
method.text: A model at 99% in validation is only a start: I go and measure the gap in real conditions, and I look for its cause.
